subject: Taxes
title: The Jacquerie
description: A quick, practical guide to The Jacquerie.

hook.text: In 1358, French peasants exploded in fury. Nobles taxed them for ransoms after losing battles.

buildup.text: After the Battle of Poitiers, France's nobles were captured.

discovery.text: The Jacquerie erupted in northern France. Peasants burned castles and killed noble families in a frenzy of rage.

twist.text: Nobles crushed the revolt with extreme violence, killing 20,000. But they quietly reduced taxes afterward.

climax.text: The Jacquerie proved that suppressing revolts doesn't fix the cause. You can kill rebels, but the grievance remains.

punchline.text: Peasants burned castles. Nobles killed 20,000. Taxes quietly dropped.

quiz.question: What triggered the Jacquerie revolt in France?
options: Ransom and war taxes on peasants
